implementation: The opt-in shared replay owns five distinct allocations for shared input, gate weights, up weights, activated input and down weights, totalling54263808 bytes. Each live surface is refreshed before norm/correction consumers in the original shared stream. Shared correction bounds point to these allocations and select the existing lossless staged2 four-lane dot. Routed arenas, original norm scans, candidate predicates, activations and arithmetic helpers are unchanged. The default remains disabled and only the existing supported shared prevalidated q8192 route may activate it.
ownership_validation: The actual extracted allocation, preparation, dispatch and ordered-release code is tested on the host. All ten interleaved flag/operand allocation failures and success are checked, with drain failure forbidding every free. Five surface shapes, repeated refreshes, empty/mismatched dimensions, absent views, preparation errors and invalid shared state are rejected as required. Actual shared gate/up/down dispatch arguments select separate shared pointers and reject missing operands; disabled mode preserves the original pointers and route.
numerical_scope: Twelve generated shared shapes include sparse, dense and exceptional candidates, both K2048 and K512, and six complete q8192 shapes. Independent CPU original dots define77 repeating input/weight classes per shape. Every output BF16 value, original norm bit, eligibility flag, prepared word, original input, synthetic producer input and guard is checked after each warmup and measurement. Control prepared storage remains untouched. Four original routed comparisons and two norm scans recheck routing and arithmetic independently. Generated producer fixtures are not model inference or a GB10 continuation.
timing_scope: One warmup and three rotated completed measurements per shared variant. Timers include original norm and eligibility scans, optional lossless operand preparation, actual existing shared correction dispatch, and completion. Allocation, reset, transfers and checking are outside component clocks. The provider build separately records retained AOT identities and binary provenance. Product decisions require a real q8192 GB10-attached comparison.
decision: Native correctness and ownership checks pass. Generated ordinary and dense q8192 cases regress while exceptional cases improve. Proceed to a bounded same-DLL real-model disabled/enabled comparison to determine whether actual shared operands and candidate distribution benefit. No package or performance acceptance is inferred.
